memory_update.text: Direct AI accelerator public-market leaders for this node: NVDA, AMD, AVGO, MRVL.
Critical upstream capacity enablers for AI accelerators/custom ASICs: TSM, ASML, AMAT, KLAC, LRCX.
EDA/IP beneficiaries of custom AI ASIC proliferation: SNPS, CDNS, ARM.
HBM and memory bandwidth should be tracked as part of the AI accelerator node; MU is the main US-listed HBM supplier, while key non-US comparables include SK hynix and Samsung.
Rack-scale conversion layer candidates include SMCI and DELL because accelerator supply must be integrated into deployable servers with power, cooling, networking, and service support.

Important non-US or less directly US-listed exposures not included in the 15-candidate cap: SK hynix, Samsung Electronics, ASE Technology, Global Unichip, Alchip, Wistron, Quanta Computer, Inventec, Wiwynn, Foxconn Industrial Internet, and Advantest.

Additional US-listed second-order candidates for later layers: ANET for AI Ethernet networking, TER for semiconductor test automation, AEHR as a smaller test/burn-in exception candidate, HPE for enterprise AI systems, and ORCL/MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL/META as demand-side customers/custom silicon owners.

Primary falsification checks: accelerator revenue fails to convert into cash/profit, custom ASIC demand is concentrated in too few customers, HBM/CoWoS constraints ease faster than expected, hyperscalers overbuild capacity, or server integrators show backlog without margin/cash conversion.

node: AI accelerators, GPUs, XPUs, and custom ASIC silicon
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the AI accelerator and custom ASIC silicon node. The highest-direct-exposure names are merchant accelerator vendors, custom silicon/networking ASIC suppliers, foundry/advanced-packaging enablers, EDA/IP suppliers, semiconductor capital equipment vendors, HBM memory suppliers, and AI server integration platforms. The chokepoint hypothesis remains that constraints can shift from visible GPU supply into HBM attach, CoWoS/advanced packaging, reticle/foundry capacity, EDA/IP, wafer-processing equipment, test/burn-in, and rack-level deployment readiness.
